study_identification_part.si_4_title: Charting brain growth and aging at high spatial precision

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Warped Bayesian Linear Regression (WBLR) was used with a sinarcsinsh warping function to model non-Gaussian effects. The model used a B-spline basis expansion (cubic spline with five evenly spaced knots) for non-linear age effects, and site variation was modeled using fixed effects.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Bayesian Linear Regression (BLR) with likelihood warping was used to predict cortical thickness and subcortical volume from a vector of covariates (age, sex, and site). ... A likelihood warping approach was used to model non-Gaussian effects. This involves applying a bijective non-linear warping function to the non-Gaussian response variables to map them to a Gaussian latent space where inference can be performed in closed form. We employed a 'sinarcsinsh' warping function

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness values from the Destrieux parcellation (148 cortical regions, 74 per hemisphere) and subcortical volumetric values from aseg.stats were modeled. Total of 188 brain regions were included.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: we fit normative models for cortical thickness and subcortical volumes derived from Freesurfer (version 6.0). ... Freesurfer functions aparcstats2table and asegstats2table were run to extract cortical thickness from the Destrieux parcellation and subcortical volume for all participants

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age was modeled with a B-spline basis expansion (cubic spline with five evenly spaced knots) to capture non-linear effects. Sex was included as a covariate. Site was modeled as fixed effects to account for scanner/site variation across 82 sites.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we fit normative models using a set of covariates (age, sex, and fixed effects for site) to predict cortical thickness and subcortical volume ... consisting of a B-spline basis expansion (cubic spline with five evenly spaced knots) to model nonlinear effects of age ... Site variation was modeled using fixed effects
